disposition.bigger_shape:
Two pieces, neither a private read-callback mode in FileReader.

(1) Layer, as asked on #36316 and the route the open user issues on these streams (#26505, #11011) need: child.stdout and child.stderr become fd-backed net.Socket, as stdio[3+] already is. In ChildProcess#spawn start the 'pipe' -> 'socket-fd' loop at /workspace/bun/src/js/node/child_process.ts:1428 at slot 1, return require('node:net').connect({ fd }) from #getBunSpawnIo (the arm ending at :1341) while keeping the #closesNeeded / once('close') wiring, and lift the i < 3 guards at /workspace/bun/src/runtime/api/bun/spawn/stdio.rs:419-423, /workspace/bun/src/spawn_sys/spawn_process.rs:921-923, /workspace/bun/src/runtime/api/bun/subprocess/Readable.rs:147 and the NULL slots at /workspace/bun/src/runtime/api/bun/subprocess.rs:770-772; or take #29141's Pipe handle. Rough size: 100 to 250 src lines (lane estimate, unbuilt) and no new FileReader or event-loop primitive, since net.ts pushDataToSocket already reports a listener throw as uncaughtException. It is not drop-in: it needs the maintainer go-ahead that was never given, and these gaps settled with it: child 'exit' and 'close' ahead of the pipe's 'data' (stdio[3] printed exit,close with no 'data' 12/12 in /tmp/disp/exitorder.cjs, where Node prints data,exit,end,close) and 'end'/'close' still reached after a fatal throw at hangup (the ground of open #33614 and #34661), Node's process lifetime for unread pipes (#41632), about +18 syscalls per spawn plus a one-time node:net load (lane-measured, not re-run by me), and Windows slots 1-2 (which #47776 moves onto the POSIX 'socket-fd' code).

yes.argument: Every surviving item argues against merging this head as it stands, so the evidence gives my side no endorsement of the merge; what it gives is the defect, the direction and the demand. The defect is real and shipped: the skeptics who ran it reproduced, on Bun 1.3.13, 1.4.2 and the merge-base build, a throwing 'data' listener on child.stdout that skips the program's 'uncaughtException' handler and exits 1, or stalls the stream with the child blocked in write, and they saw the PR build print the same events as Node v26.3.0 (items 6, 8, 9, 13, 14; my re-run of the cited /tmp/frame/stall.cjs hung 6 of 7 times on the base build and 0 of 7 on the PR build). It was never a decision: item 10 traces the wrong channel to a 2022 perf commit and shows that maintainers already merged the opposite contract, for process.stdin in #34019 (/workspace/bun/test/js/node/process/process-stdin.test.ts:388, "a throw from a 'data' listener is an uncaughtException, and stdin keeps reading"), for promise-dispatched callbacks in #34660, and as the rule at /workspace/bun/REVIEW.md:48, "Invoke user callbacks through event_loop.runCallback". The mechanism is Node's own read-callback contract rather than an invention: item 12 notes that readStart, onRead and kReading restate Node's _read, onStreamRead and readStop logic, and the skeptic who tested the diff against Node's source wrote "Keep the core (native read callback through the event loop); it is the Node direction and is verified" (item 5). The "no user report" objection covers only the headline symptom: items 4 and 7 concede that the same root cause has a user-filed open issue, #48514, and that dropping this work would lose that stall and two more child-stdio stalls that the read-callback path fixes (the deterministic #48514 probe stalled 3 of 3 times on the base build and 0 of 3 on the PR build when I re-ran it). The blocker is an unanswered question, not a veto: the one maintainer sentence was a conditional request on a net.Socket-facade PR whose data path was unchanged, the author's "Want me to go ahead?" got no answer, the fd route has no prototype for stdout and stderr, and its own advocates price it at +18 syscalls and +104 K instructions per spawn plus a node:net load, with 'exit' before 'data' in 19 of 20 runs still to fix, though item 12 shows it is cheaper per chunk (items 1, 2, 9, 11, 12). This path, by contrast, has no public surface and a single opt-in call site, so it can be removed if sockets arrive, and its tests are "worth keeping either way" (items 3, 6). None of the fourteen items recommends dropping the work (item 7: "neither merge this head nor drop the work"); each asks for a maintainer ruling or pre-merge fixes, so maintainers who have twice merged this contract have reason to want this change to exist as the built, measured option for that ruling, once item 5's cross-pipe 'end' ordering (which I confirmed: stderr is empty at stdout 'close' on the PR build, 68 bytes on the base build and Node) and item 10's lifetime test are fixed.

frame.proposed_change: A Node-compat bug fix, delivered as a new native delivery path for the stdout and stderr pipes of node:child_process. Today child.stdout and child.stderr are NativeReadables whose _read() pulls the native FileReader (ptr.pull()). push(), and so emit('data'), runs inside _read() or inside the pull promise's reaction. A listener throw on the promise path becomes an unhandledRejection and nothing reads again: no 'end', no 'close', the child blocks in write, the parent hangs. After the change, ChildProcess#getBunSpawnIo passes handleMode = true to constructNativeReadable, which registers a callback through a new internal method FileInternalReadableStreamSource.setReadCallback (kept in a new readCallback internal field of the wrapper). FileReader then runs in "handle mode": a new event-loop task (task_tag::FileReaderReadStart) starts its pipe reader from spawn on, and each read completion calls the callback as a top-level event-loop call through new EventLoop::run_callback_then: cb(chunk) with a Buffer that owns its bytes (allocation adopted when at least half full, else one copy), cb(null) at EOF, cb(undefined, err) on a read error. The call runs inside the AsyncLocalStorage context captured at spawn (new Bun__enterAsyncContextOfCallback / Bun__leaveAsyncContextOfCallback) and is followed by a nextTick and microtask checkpoint. false from the callback pauses the reader until _read() calls setFlowing(true) (new PosixFlags::PAUSE_ENDS_READ_LOOP, WindowsBufferedReader::try_unpause).…[+2371c]
beliefs_for_yes: The failure is real on main and in a shipped release: when a chunk of child.stdout/child.stderr arrives on a pending pull, a throw from the 'data' listener is reported as unhandledRejection and the stream never reads again (no 'end', no 'close', the child blocks in write, the parent hangs while something keeps it alive). Check: /tmp/frame/stall.cjs and /tmp/frame/throw1.cjs on Bun 1.4.2, a main build and the PR build. Seen here: stall.cjs hung 5 of 6 runs on 1.4.2 and 6 of 6 on /tmp/rel/bun-base, 0 of 6 on /tmp/rel/bun-arm; 1.3.13 already reports unhandledRejection and emits no 'end' or 'close'.

Node's observed behaviour is what the PR targets: with an 'uncaughtException' handler the throw reaches it and the stream goes on to 'end' and 'close'; with none the process exits 1 at the throw. Check: the same scripts plus /tmp/frame/throw2.cjs under Node v26.3.0. Seen here: the PR build and Node emit the same events in the same order.

The unhandledRejection channel is an accident of NativeReadable's pull promise, not a decision. On main the same throw is already an uncaughtException when the chunk is pushed synchronously inside _read() (1 of 6 runs of stall.cjs on 1.4.2), on process.stdin over a pipe (/tmp/frame/stdin.cjs) and on stdio[3+] net.Sockets (/tmp/frame/fd3.cjs). Check: git grep unhandledRejection in test/js/node/child_process and test/js/bun/spawn at 447ff870b60 finds no test that pins it for child stdio.

The bug is worth about 600 lines of native and built-in code although nobody outside the bot has reported it. Tracker searches here for child_process stdout with 'data' listener throw, uncaughtException, unhandledRejection or hang found no user issue; the sources are robobun's own PRs #37171, #43790 and #48551, and the merged precedent for the bug class is #34660 (fs/dns/pbkdf2 callbacks, guardCallback). Check: an issue search, and whether a real program (an exec/execFile wrapper, a test runner with an uncaughtException handler) has hit the hang.

A catch at the emit or push boundary cannot meet the requirements. That is the shape #34660 merged as guardCallback, the pushed head of #37171 (9006a439fb2, +37/-18 in src) and origin/robobun/f00c9907/rework-clean (+56/-27 in src). The claim against it: it keeps the pull promise, reads on after a fatal report so a child.on('close', code => process.exit(code)) wrapper exits 0, swallows a throw from a manual emit('data') or read(), and guards one of two emit sites. Check: run this diff's new tests (the 'no uncaughtException handler' group and the 'order' group) against those two branches.

A process.nextTick push cannot meet them either: a listener that removes itself and re-attaches from a promise job loses a chunk, and 'end' runs before an async listener's continuation. Check: tests 'a listener that removes itself and comes back from a promise job misses no chunk' and 'a chunk and the EOF that are already in the pipe wait for the listener's tick and promise job' against a tick-based prototype (#48551 is the nearest open one).

This is a better vehicle than the design the only maintainer review in this PR family asked for. Jarred-Sumner, CHANGES_REQUESTED on #36316 (2026-07-29): 'can we instead make it so stdout and stderr are file descriptors we then pass to net.Socket?', and '@robobun adopt' on #26505. stdio[3+] already takes that route on main and delivers a listener throw as uncaughtException. The PR's case against it is +18 syscalls per spawn, loading node:net, and POSIX only. Check: no prototype of that design is visible among the remote branches, so the +18 needs its fixture (rough probe here with /tmp/m/sysc: two additional net.Socket-wrapped stdio slots cost about +35 syscalls per spawn on main, which includes two more socketpairs). Ask whether the maintainers still want that design: if so, handle mode is a stopgap it deletes on POSIX, and the bot's own #41632 calls its change 'the stopgap' for that reason.

The new shared primitives are warranted, minimal and not duplicates: EventLoop::run_callback_then with CallbackOutcome (a third variant beside run_callback and run_callback_with_result, whose 'never from a host function' contract is enforced only by a doc comment), PosixFlags::PAUSE_ENDS_READ_LOOP, WindowsBufferedReader::try_unpause, task_tag::FileReaderReadStart (COUNT 86 to 87), Bun__enterAsyncContextOfCallback / Bun__leaveAsyncContextOfCallback in a new ReadCallbackAsyncContext.cpp, and the readCallback internal field. REVIEW.md: 'New cross-cutting abstractions need maintainer agreement before appearing inside a feature PR.' Check: grep for an existing entry that reports a call's outcome ahead of the microtask checkpoint, or that enters a stored callback's async context around its error report; each new item has one caller.

This is the PR to take, and a merge order exists, among the open robobun PRs that rewrite the same functions of native-readable.ts and child_process.ts: #48553 (its kRemainingChunk hunk is carried in this diff), #48551 (makes _read() a readStart for every native Readable and claims to fix user issue #48514), #43790, #44849, #41632, #48635, #48652. Check: gh pr list for 'native-readable' and 'child stdio'; trial-merge each onto 8ad649dafc8; decide whether #48553 lands first so that hunk leaves this diff; run #48514's repro on macOS against this head (it did not stall on Linux on either build here).

Only node:child_process stdout and stderr opt in, and nothing else changes behaviour or cost. constructNativeReadable(..., true) has one caller (child_process.ts:1309) and setReadCallback one (registerReadCallback); the method sits on the internal source wrapper behind the private $bunNativePtr slot, so there is no public API or bun-types change. Readable.fromWeb keeping unhandledRejection matches Node. Check: grep those two names; the fromWeb test added to node-stream.test.js; /tmp/frame/fromweb.mjs (seen here: Node also reports unhandledRejection and stalls); the three pull-path fixtures in /tmp/m. Shared code that did change for every FileReader user: the extra ref release in FileReader::on_cancel and the exit condition of PosixBufferedReader::read_loop.

Keeping main's process lifetime is right for this PR even though it is neither Node's nor Bun 1.3's. An unref'd child whose pipes nothing reads holds the parent for 0 s on main and with the PR, and 2 s on Node and on Bun 1.3.13; open PR #41632 calls main's behaviour a 1.4.0 regression from #34971. Check: /tmp/frame/life.cjs plain|touch|data (seen here for 'plain': 1.3.13 2.0 s, 1.4.2 0.0 s, base 0.0 s, PR 0.0 s, Node 2.0 s). The kUnread list and unref-until-first-_read() exist only to preserve main's answer, so this should be decided together with #41632.

Reading from spawn on, up to one highWaterMark per pipe into a JS list before anything reads the stream, does not undo the kernel backpressure that #34971 and #36035 introduced with lazy pipes, and memory stays bounded per child. Check: existing tests 'stdout pipe backpressure > blocks the child until a reader attaches and delivers every byte' and 'child.stdout.pause() after flowing stops native reads and blocks the child' (both pass on the PR release build here); RSS of many children that write and are never read.

The other changes every child_process program will see match Node and break no Bun user: each chunk owns its ArrayBuffer and chunk sizes change (1 GiB arrived in 14.9 to 16.0 K chunks on the base build, 12.0 to 13.6 K on the PR build); a listener's nextTicks run before its promise jobs and both before the next chunk or 'end'; 'data' listeners and the uncaughtException report see the AsyncLocalStorage store of the spawn, not of where the listener was attached. Check: /tmp/frame/als.cjs (seen here: 1.4.2 and the base build print 'the listener attach', the PR build and Node v26.3.0 print 'the spawn'); the 'order' tests; a search for code that relies on a shared chunk.buffer or on the old store.

The two other child_process.ts hunks are required by the fix and regress nothing: stdout and stderr are built at spawn for stdio arrays shorter than 3, and after a spawn error an already-built stream is resumed and drained instead of being marked 'destroyed'. Check: tests 'stdout and stderr of a 2-entry stdio array' and 'a listener attached late'; the ENOENT/EACCES spawn-error tests; per-spawn syscall and instruction counts with a 2-entry stdio array (the PR's per-spawn numbers use default stdio, which main already builds eagerly).

With no handler, pausing the reader and resuming it on the loop's next turn (FileReader::wait_for_next_turn, enqueue_task_after_yield) is a sound way to get 'listener runs once, no end, no close, exit code 1' under bun run and bun -e. It holds because is_event_loop_alive_excluding_immediates() is false once unhandled_error_counter > 0 (src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs). Check: the tests under "throw from a child stdio 'data' listener with no 'uncaughtException' handler" and /tmp/frame/r1c.cjs (seen here: 'exit; data 1' and status 1 on the base build, the PR build and Node).

Where Bun's loop keeps turning after a fatal report (a pending top-level await, a setImmediate loop, --hot, bun test, the REPL), it is acceptable that the stream goes on, the listener is called again and 'close' fires, so `process.exit(await closeCode)` exits 0 after a fatal listener throw. repl.test.ts pins this on purpose ("a top-level await of the child's 'close' resumes"). Check: /tmp/frame/r1b.mjs and `/tmp/frame/r1a.cjs immediate` (seen here, 3 of 3 runs: base build hangs, status 124; PR build prints 'data 1; data 2; end; child close 0' and exits 0; Node prints 'data 1' and exits 1).

Carrying that mechanism now is better than waiting for #34661 (cirospaciari, open since 2026-07-18: an uncaught error that nothing takes ends the run at the report), which would make waits_for_next_turn, the held end and error, and the exit-0 cases of the previous belief moot. Check: state and review of #34661; whether wait_for_next_turn and its flag delete cleanly once the report exits.

Residual (c) may stay out of scope: a listener attached in the child's 'exit' that throws fatally is still followed by 'end' and 'close', so a close wrapper exits 0. Check: /tmp/frame/r1d.cjs (seen here: status 0 on the base and PR builds, 1 on Node), and that a tracking issue is filed (REVIEW.md: 'out of scope without a tracker is not accepted').

Lifetimes and re-entrancy are sound. The callback lives only in the wrapper's readCallback slot (no Strong, so the stream-wrapper cycle stays collectable) while the across-read ref keeps the wrapper alive; destroy(), cancel(), a nested event-loop tick or a VM stop from inside the callback, GC of an unread stream, and a task released unrun leave the refcounts balanced. Check: the four test files on the debug+ASAN build with BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks=1; a spawn/drop/Bun.gc(true) stress loop with heapStats; pairing queue_read_start's ref with run_read_start and release_unrun, and on_cancel's new decrement with on_reader_done and wrapper_finalized.

Windows and macOS behave like Linux and CI is green on every lane. None of that is known yet: the Windows branches (the reader ignores false from on_read_chunk; pause() and try_unpause()) compiled but never ran, `bun run rust:check-all` is pending, and 8ad649dafc8 has not been pushed, so no CI has run on this head. Check: push, then read the per-job results for the four test files on Windows, macOS x64 and arm64, musl and ASAN.

The performance claims hold and nothing measured regresses: per paced chunk 13 to 5 GC cells, 3 to 2 recvfrom, 55.9 K to 47.3 K instructions; 1 GiB gapless 710 M to 607 M; per spawn no increase; other FileReader consumers unchanged; text +12,158 bytes; FileReader gains four Cell<bool>. Check: rerun the fixtures in /tmp/m with both release binaries (seen here: 1 GiB gapless 682 to 737 M against 437 to 526 M user instructions, two runs each) and on macOS and Windows. Caveat to settle first: /tmp/rel/bun-base reports revision dbcb23530, a merge commit of the earlier catch-at-emit attempt, not 447ff870b60. It behaved like 1.4.2 in the probes above, but the baseline should be a build whose revision is on main.

The tests are valid, stable and affordable. The four files fail on main and pass on the PR (seen here with the release builds on child_process.test.ts: 13 new tests fail on the base build and pass on the PR build; 'spawn still works with more than 10240 fds open' fails on both; 16 s on the PR build; the other three files were not run here). The order and count tests ('per chunk the stream queues one tick, and makes no promise and no Buffer but the chunk') must not flake under debug+ASAN. Existing tests that reached FileReader's pull path through child.stdout must keep their coverage (the nested-pull use-after-free regression was widened to Readable.fromWeb(Bun.spawn().stdout); spawn-stdout-iterate-leak.fixture.ts needs a look). The vendored Node tests test-child-process-*, test-stdio-* and test-stream-* must still pass. Check: each file on both builds, repeats under ASAN, the node parallel suite.

The size and scope are acceptable for one PR: +599/-37 in 10 src files and +1565/-50 in 4 test files, against +37/-18 and +56/-27 src lines for the two catch prototypes, and two concerns if the #48553 hunk counts. REVIEW.md: 'Diff size itself is grounds for changes-requested' and 'If a maintainer doesn't understand your logic after one explanation, simplify rather than justify.' Check: whether a reviewer can state, from the code alone, the invariants of the five interacting FileReader flags (read_callback, flowing, read_start_queued, arming, waits_for_next_turn) and of kReading and kUnread in native-readable.ts.
